newsitem.title: FRANCE: French spy service coders seek Jospin mediation.
newsitem.headline: French spy service coders seek Jospin mediation.

text.p: Striking Foreign Ministry coders, who scramble France's top secret mail to keep it from spies, on Monday appealed to Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to mediate over threats to replace some of them with computers.
The encryption experts have been on indefinite strike for 12 days over management plans to shed 80 of 450 posts. They also staged a five-day stoppage in May.

"We appeal for the arbitration of the prime minister," the coders said in a statement. "In the plans of our management, what will become of the safety of communications and the confidentiality of government transmissions?".
The Foreign Ministry reckons that computers have made some of the human jobs obsolete but has promised that cuts will be carried out without sackings.
The experts have been guaranteeing a skeleton service encoding and decoding messages between Paris and French embassies around the world and between government ministries.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said the strike meant messages were being processed more slowly than normal but insisted it had not led to any security problems.
Jospin came to power two weeks ago after President Jacques Chirac's centre-right allies lost a snap National Assembly election.
